_doc: The Almanac's Land and Sky page (core/land_sky.gd): one idea per row, noted once any of its flags is set (a Gazetteer plaque's plaque_<id>, a flag an NPC sets, or a tally such as forecast_passes). Keep each note to one true thing in plain words, under about 80 characters: the ledger shows it on one line.

ideas.title: Basalt columns
ideas.note: Slow-cooling lava cracks into hexagons; the Causeway and Staffa are one flow.

ideas.title: Sea stacks
ideas.note: Cave, arch, stack, stump: the Old Man of Hoy is 137 metres of it.

ideas.title: Chalk
ideas.note: Tiny algae skeletons; rain soaks through it to feed England's chalk streams.

ideas.title: The Jurassic Coast
ideas.note: 95 miles of Dorset and Devon, 185 million years, read first by Mary Anning.

ideas.title: Eryri's volcanoes
ideas.note: Yr Wyddfa is 450-million-year-old volcanic ash with sea shells near the top.

ideas.title: Limestone pavement
ideas.note: Ice scraped it bare, rain ate the cracks into grykes; now protected by law.

ideas.title: Peat and carbon
ideas.note: Wet peat locks carbon away a millimetre a year; drained peat gives it back.

ideas.title: The jet stream
ideas.note: A river of wind miles up that steers the Atlantic lows at Britain.

ideas.title: The North Atlantic Drift
ideas.note: Warm Gulf water keeps the west mild enough for palms in Cornwall.

ideas.title: The Shipping Forecast
ideas.note: 31 sea areas in a set order: wind, weather, visibility. Gale is force 8.

ideas.title: Highs and lows
ideas.note: Air rises in a low (rain), sinks in a high (settled). Low on your left.

ideas.title: The Met Office
ideas.note: Founded 1854 under Robert FitzRoy, who coined the word forecast. Home: Exeter.

ideas.title: A warming climate
ideas.note: 40.3C at Coningsby, 19 July 2022; CO2 up from 280 to over 420 parts per million.

ideas.title: Rewilding
ideas.note: Let the land run itself: Knepp's storks, Devon's beavers, bog pools on the moor.
